source_text: Properties of schemes local in the fppf topology

<STRUCT_0001>
In this section we find some properties of schemes which are local on the base
in the fppf topology.

The property <MATH_0001>``<MATH_0002> is locally Noetherian'' is local
in the fppf topology.

We will use Lemma <REF_0001>.
First we note that ``being locally Noetherian'' is local
in the Zariski topology. This is clear from the definition,
see Properties, Definition <REF_0002>.
Next, we show that if <MATH_0001> is a flat, finitely presented
morphism of affines and <MATH_0002> is locally Noetherian, then <MATH_0003> is
locally Noetherian. This is
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0003>.
Finally, we have to show that if <MATH_0004> is a surjective
flat, finitely presented morphism of affines and <MATH_0005> is
locally Noetherian, then <MATH_0006> is locally Noetherian. This follows from
Algebra, Lemma <REF_0004>.
Thus (1), (2) and (3) of Lemma <REF_0005> hold
and we win.

The property <MATH_0001>``every quasi-compact open of <MATH_0002>
has a finite number of irreducible components'' is local
in the fppf topology.

We will use Lemma <REF_0001>. First we note that
<MATH_0001> is local in the Zariski topology.
Next, we show that if <MATH_0002> is a flat, finitely presented

Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0002>.
Hence it suffices to show that for <MATH_0008> the fibre <MATH_0009>
has a finite number of generic points. Note that <MATH_0010> is an

Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0003>.
Hence <MATH_0012> is Noetherian and has a finite number of irreducible components

Properties, Lemma <REF_0005>).
